result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.all_pairs_shortest_path()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute shortest paths for all pairs of nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L17887-L17965){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.all_pairs_shortest_path() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Uses Dijkstra's algorithm from each source node to find the shortest path to all other reachable nodes. Returns the full path as a list of node IDs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, dict[int, list[int]]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Nested dictionary where `result[source][target] = path` (list of node IDs from source to target, inclusive). Only includes reachable pairs. Unreachable pairs are omitted. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Time complexity: `O(n * (m + n) * log(n))` where `n` is nodes and `m` is edges. Space complexity: `O(n² * average_path_length)` for storing all paths. This method stores full paths, which can be memory intensive for large graphs. If you only need distances, use `all_pairs_shortest_path_length()` instead. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Simple path graph: ::: {#7097927c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(4) # Creates 1-2-3-4 paths = graph.all_pairs_shortest_path() paths[1][4], paths[2][4] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ([1, 2, 3, 4], [2, 3, 4]) ``` ::: ::: Weighted graph with multiple routes: ::: {#d4bed20b .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(weighted=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=1.0) .add_edge(source="B", target="D", weight=1.0) .add_edge(source="A", target="C", weight=1.0) .add_edge(source="C", target="D", weight=5.0) ) paths = graph.all_pairs_shortest_path() a_id = graph.get_id_from_label("A") d_id = graph.get_id_from_label("D") # the cheaper A->B->D route is chosen over A->C->D paths[a_id][d_id] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [1, 2, 4] ``` ::: ::: In a star graph, every path between two leaves must pass through the center, since that's the only node connecting them: ::: {#0d598a2c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_star_graph(5) # Star with center node 1 paths = graph.all_pairs_shortest_path() node_ids = graph.get_node_ids() center = 1 leaves = [n for n in node_ids if n != center] all( center in paths[source][target] for source in leaves for target in leaves if source < target ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: :::
